Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from this game! The result has panned out how everyone expected it to. Pakistan win the first game of the tri-series and quite convincingly. They now face a tougher challenge as they will take on Australia on the 2nd of July at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Till then, goodbye and take care.

Pakistan skipper, Sarfraz Ahmed, says they were eager to win the first game and they have done so. Credits the way Zaman played at the start and Asif played at the end. He feels the ball was coming onto the bat nicely but there was movement at the beginning. Admits they were quite lethargic in the field but their bowlers did the job for them. Ends by saying plenty of cricket is left and he hopes to do well.

Asif Ali has been awarded the Man of the Match for his power-hitting. He finished with 41 from just 21 balls and provided Pakistan the much-needed impetus they needed. Strangely, he does not have an interview with Alistair Campbell.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza, says that a poor Powerplay put them under pressure and they were never in the game during the chase. He feels Pakistan scored 20 runs extra which was a lot on this wicket. Ends by saying they failed to execute their plans but they need not change anything as of now.

Pakistan bowling once again was at its best. Mohammad Nawaz along with his opening partner Usman Khan were the pick of the bowlers. The spinner provided the breakthroughs at the start and the pacer chipped in with the wickets at the end. The two combined with figures of 7-0-22-4. The rest played their part with 5 of the 7 bowlers having a wicket to their name.

A dominating display by Pakistan, justifying why exactly they are at the top of the T20I rankings. To be honest, it was all set up by their batsmen as they gave the hosts a target which according to me was above par on this surface. Chasing 183, the top order had to fire for Zimbabwe but that was not the case. They lost two in the Powerplay with not many on the board. Mire and Musakanda, the latter who was their top scorer, did try to bring the chase back on track but wickets at regular intervals saw them get nowhere close to where they had to be at the end.

OUT! That is it! Hafeez finishes things off as he gets two in his only over. This is nicely tossed up on off, it turns back in. Muzarabani throws the kitchen sink at it but does not connect. The ball hits the top of middle. PAKISTAN WIN BY 74 RUNS!
Worked with the turn through mid-wicket for a run.
Driven towards the mid off region.
John Nyumbu is the last man in.

OUT! Hafeez too has a wicket to his name! Burl tries to be innovative and goes for the reverse sweep. Hafeez gives him no pace to work with. Burl still goes ahead with the shot, he gets a top edge which balloons to short third man where Malik runs to his right and accepts a dolly.
Floats this up on off, Burl makes room and hits it over covers for a brace.
Mohammad Hafeez is into the attack.
Fuller on middle, Muzarabani works it to mid-wicket.
Blessing Muzarabani is the new man in. Meanwhile, the on-air commentators inform us that Kyle Jarvis is not available for batting as he is in the hospital now.

OUT! Second in the over for Khan! This is a brilliant delivery, not a lot the tailender could have done about it. On a length around off, this one straightens after pitching. Chisoro goes back and tries to keep it out but the ball takes the outside edge and goes into the mitts of the keeper.
Hits it hard down to long on for a run.
A yorker on off, the batsman digs it out towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Comes down the track and flashes at a ball outside off, it goes towards sweeper cover for a run.

OUT! No fifty for Musakanda as he falls 7 runs short. Usman gets his first. It is on a length around off, TM goes for the heave but only gets a top edge which goes high up in the air towards Shadab at mid off. He runs back and takes a neat catch.
Usman Khan to bowl the 17th over.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Fuller on middle, Musakanda hits it through mid-wicket and the batsmen run two.
Slower ball and wide of the off stump. TM goes after it but does not connect.
On a length around off, Burl tries to pull but gets an inside edge which falls just short of the keeper. He makes a half-stop and the batsmen sneak through for a run.
On the shorter side, Musakanda pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
On a length around off, the batsman guides it through point for a run.
Faheem Ashraf is back on.
Fullish ball, swept away to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Good running! Musakanda taps this one towards the vacant wide mid on region and calls for the second run. Shadab himself runs after it but fails to stop the couple.
On a flatter trajectory and shorter in length, Ryan mistimes his pull to short fine leg. A run taken.
Slow through the air, worked gently to mid-wicket.
Floated ball, Musakanda plays it against the spin to mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up delivery on a fullish length, Burl leans ahead and eases it to long off for a run.
Shadab Khan returns for a bowl.
Shorter outside off, Burl chops it towards cover-point for a run.
Good length on off, defended.
Ryan Burl makes his way out at no. 7.

OUT! TIMBER! One shot too many by Chigumbura! Half the side back in the hut for Zimbabwe. The change of pace does the trick for Hasan Ali. It is a well-disguised slower ball on off, Chigumbura is way too early into the shot. He misses and the ball shatters the off stump.
FOUR! Up and over! Chigumbura is not going down without a fight! Full and on off, Chigumbura slams it over mid off. A boundary results. 10 from the last two deliveries.
SIX! He has picked the bones out of that one! Short and on the chest of the batsman. Elton stands tall and smacks it over the mid-wicket fence.
WIDE! A bumper but a little too high and the umpire calls it a wide.

Direct hit needed... but the fielder misses! Musakanda was out by a long way had he hit. Chigumbura hits it towards mid off. Musakanda wants a run but is sent back by his partner. He turns to make it back but collides with the bowler and falls onto the ground. Hasan Ali also shows good sportsman spirit by not taking the bails off as he helps the batsman back on his feet.
Hasan Ali is back on.

The arm ball on off, the batsman tries to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and goes to the man at short fine leg and the batsmen take a run. Nawaz finishes his spell with brilliant figures of, 4-0-11-2.
Fires it on off, Chigumbura keeps it out.
Whips it through mid-wicket with the angle and gets a brace.
On the stumps, kept out.
Flatter but on the shorter side, Musakanda pulls it through mid-wicket for another run.
Down the leg side, Chigumbura tries to flick but the ball brushes the pads and goes towards short fine leg. The batsmen run a leg bye.
Good length on off, the batsman taps it towards covers for a run.
Fuller in length on middle, Musakanda drives it down to long on for a run.
A bumper outside off, Musakanda tries to drag his pull but does not connect.

In the air, but safe! Down the leg side, Musakanda tries to flick. The ball takes the edge and goes high up in the air. It clears the man at mid-wicket who turns and runs towards it but does not get to it. Two taken.
Shortish ball, angling in, pulled to the leg side.
FOUR! Creamed! Short and on middle, Chigumbura stands tall and pulls it with authority through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Elton Chigumbura walks out to the middle.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Shadab gets his first. Moor this time tries to clear the mid-wicket fence with a slog sweep. Shadab bowls the googly. Peter misses, the ball turns back in and knocks the off stump out.
Works it by using his wrists but finds mid-wicket.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Slightly shorter on middle, Musakanda pulls it through mid-wicket for a brace.
The googly on middle, Moor tries to drive but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a run.
Walks across his stumps, flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. Another tight over by Nawaz comes to an end. His figures now read, 3-0-7-2.
Flicks it through the same region for a run.
Worked with the angle to mid-wicket.
Peter Moor is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... taken! Mire holes out in an attempt to up the ante. He had no choice, had to go for it with the run rate increasing on every ball. Nawaz tosses it up outside off, it turns away. Mire goes for the slog sweep but the ball takes the top edge. It goes high up in the air just over mid-wicket. Hasan there, backtracks, judges it nicely and then takes it. Mire fails to convert another start and Zimbabwe are now staring down the barrel.
The batsman moves in his crease to upset the line and length of the bowler. Nawaz sticks to bowling on the stumps. Musakanda sweeps it through square leg for a run.
The batsman makes room and the bowler follows him. He can only push it to covers for a run.
Mohammad Nawaz is back on.
Flicks it through mid-wicket and bags a brace. 10 from this over and 21 from the last two.
On the stumps, kept out.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. One run added to the total.
Flatter on off, Mire guides it to short third man.

SIX! Shades of ABD in that! Mire goes down on one knee early and then with the help of his wrists sweeps it behind the square leg region. The connection is such that the ball travels all the way. The two now have decided to step on the pedal.
Musakanda gets into position early there and plays the sweep shot. He finds the fielder in the deep square leg region and a single results.

No, they can't! Just a single from the last ball but a good over for the hosts. They need a few more of these. On a length around middle, Musakanda works it through mid-wicket for a run. 138 more needed in 72 balls.
FOUR! Very classy! This is fuller on off, Musakanda strokes it through mid off and the ball races to the fence. 10 from the over with a ball to go. Can they make this a 14 or a 16-run over?
Shorter in length on middle, Musakanda pulls it through square leg for another couple.
Goes fuller again and on the pads, the batsman clips it through mid-wicket for a couple.

Howzzat? Not out is the answer to that question. Full and on middle, Musakanda tries to flick but misses to get hit on the front pad. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Slipping down leg.
Nicely timed! Slightly fuller on off, Musakanda times it on the up through covers for a brace.
Hussain Talat is into the attack.
Fires this full on middle, Mire goes for the sweep but gets an inside edge onto his pads. That saved him, had he missed it, he was a candidate for an LBW.
On the pads, the batsman works it around the corner for a run.
Another misfield! Pakistan are a little too lethargic in the field today. It is Shoaib Malik this time as the ball is clipped towards him at deep mid-wicket. The batsmen run two courtesy a misfield.
Another googly, Mire picks it this time. He flicks it through mid-wicket. Asif Ali in the deep misfields and the batsmen run three. Sloppy from him.
Sweeps it to deep square leg for a run.
The googly on off, Musakanda defends it onto the ground.
Shadab Khan is into the attack.

Length again on middle, Musakanda tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket for a run. Just 4 from the last over of the Powerplay. An excellent one for Pakistan. Zimbabwe need another 156 from 84 balls.
Watchfully guided down to third man for a run. They have to be watchful as they cannot afford to lose any more wickets.
Good change in pace! Bowls the slower one and on the shorter side. Mire tries to upper cut but fails to connect.
The batsman guides it to third man. One run added to the total.

Makes room and mistimes his cut towards point. The batsmen think about a run but then do not go for it. The fielder there has a needless shy at the non-striker's end and he hits the stumps. The ball deflects towards mid-wicket and the batsmen run an overthrow.
Back of a length on off, Mire defends it off the front foot.
Usman Khan is back on.
On a length around off, Musakanda keeps it out.
Down the leg side and the umpire calls it a wide.
Tarisai Musakanda strides out to the middle.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Hasan Ali has the last laugh! He bowls the sucker ball, full and way outside off. Masakadza makes room and reaches out for it with a slash. The ball takes the outside edge and goes to the keeper who takes it. Hasan does not even bother to appeal as he starts celebrating. The batsman stands his ground and then Ali turns to ask the question and the umpire raises his finger. Hamilton has to walk back cheaply and now Zimbabwe are in big trouble here.
Once again tries to play the scoop but it is a short ball and hence, Hamilton does not connect.
A typical fast bowler response! He bangs in a pacey short one on middle, Masakadza dances down and tries to pull but he misses and the ball hits him on the helmet.

SIX! WOW! What a shot! Hasan bowls it on a length around off, Hamilton goes down on one knee and scoops it. The connection is such that the ball travels all the way above the backward square leg fence.
Swing for Hasan! Something we have not seen today! On a length around off, this one shapes away. Hamilton tries to keep it out but gets beaten.
Hasan Ali is into the attack.

SIX! This time he gets all of it! First biggie of the innings. Finishes the over with a bang. The hosts needed this. It is on the fuller length, right in the zone. Mire deposits it over the long on fence. So even though there were 4 dots, 9 came from the over.

Scratch what I wrote last. This time he tries to clear the fence but gets more height than distance. It is on a length around middle, Mire goes for the heave but does not time it that well. He gets enough to clear the in-field and the batsmen run two.
Back of a length on off, Mire off the back foot defends it. He did show signs of intent in the last over to the spinner but is happy to play the fast bowler out here.
Make that three! Once again he bowls it on the body, cramping the batsman for room. Mire tries to nudge it but misses as the ball hits him on the thigh pad.
Slides this one on the pads, Mire fails to clip it and gets hit on the pads. 2 dots in a row, something has to give here.
Back of a length on middle, it comes in after pitching. Mire tries to defend it but the ball takes the inside edge and hits him on the body.
A false start by him! Down the leg side and the umpire signals it a wide.
Faheem Ashraf comes into the attack.
Stump-to-stump line, Masakadza lunges in defense. Another frugal over from Nawaz, only 2 from it.
Slow through the air, kept out watchfully.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Almost, almost another one! Coming in with the arm, Mire tries to slog sweep it across the line but misses. The ball just goes past the leg stump.
Well bowled! Mire shapes up for the reverse sweep and Nawaz bowls it down the leg side. The batsman ends up missing it.
Backs away a bit and eases it to long on for a single.

Good shot but no runs! Another ball which is on the shorter side. The batsman stands tall and pulls it hard but finds mid on. Had it been a meter to his left or right, it would have been a certain boundary.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Angles this one across the batsman. He guides it to point again.

FOUR! First boundary in the innings and it has come from the bat of Mire. Slightly shorter in length from the two previous deliveries. Mire reads the length early and pulls it hard through square leg for a boundary.
Hits the length again on off, Mire goes back and keeps it out.
Starts off with a length ball on off, the batsman defends it to point.
Usman Khan will bowl from the other end.
Hamilton Masakadza is the next man in.

OUT! Nawaz strikes! It is the straighter one from him which does the trick. He bowls it flatter on off, it comes in with the angle from off. Chibhabha who looked vulnerable against the left-arm spinner tries to work it on the leg side but misses the ball. It hits him flush on the front pad. Nawaz appeals and the umpire agrees. Hawk Eye later on confirms it was the right decision. An early blow for Zimbabwe as Chibhabha bags a duck. Not something you want when you are chasing a huge total. End of a brilliant first over by Nawaz.
Another loopy ball on middle, Chibhabha steps down the track and keeps it out.
Good bowling! This is slightly slower through the air, even Sarfraz behind the stumps liked it as he utters a word or two in appreciation in Hindi. It lands on off, Chibhabha lunges and keeps it out.
Zimbabwe are underway! Flatter and on middle, Mire goes back and tucks it around the corner with the angle for a run.
Mire looks to turn it to the leg side but is struck on the pads.
So close! Slow through the air, grips a bit on the surface. Mire checks his drive as the ball lobs in the air towards Nawaz. He moves to his left, dives but the ball falls down safely.
We are back for the run chase. Solomon Mire and Chamu Chibhabha will open the batting for Zimbabwe. Mohammad Nawaz to begin the proceedings with the ball.
